RESULT (pose-search-fields-and-forecast-review-20261022, pose-learning-repairs-decisions-20261022, pose-five-pass-design-constraints-20261022): the source repairs (S1, the decoder-inert command numbers, the forecast-pose and hand-state recording) are committed on a new branch, independently reviewed and verified by two checks (PASS). The owner's stop/save repair was rebuilt after a review found a closing-wait BLOCKER and was verified on attempt a1's saved timing (PASS, 46 of 46 conditions). The fresh attempt a2 is prepared as a DRAFT package for your package decision. No launch; supervisor pause; no trainer, owner or watcher process runs.

CORRECTION of my 5:22 PM report: the stop-schedule check (pose_learning_stop_schedule_check) tested stop_kill_at alone. In owner 1b91089e the guard (on every 5 s pass, the tree ended once stop_wait_s, 140 s, had passed since the earliest recorded stop) and the closing wait (first + stop_wait_s) still ended the trainer 140 s after the request, so the kill time I reported (4:28:05.1 PM PDT) would not have been reached. Both affected Tests rows carry a correction revision.

1. SOURCE: worktree C:/Users/bhart/Documents/UEMA_wt/s4r_pose_fields_s1_20261022, branch repair/s4r-pose-fields-s1-2026-10-22 from f0183150b (the launched checkout stays at f0183150b); commits 82dbf4d1f, 6facfeadb, 66889bdba and e058c0c81 (final).
- S1, lem_model.py differentiable_execution_transform: des_cm = des_hard.detach() + (des_soft - des_soft.detach()); pos = (cur_cm + step_hard).detach() + (step_soft - step_soft.detach()).
- Decoder-inert numbers, lem/model/physical_goal.py PhysicalTrustRegion with layout = LemLite._search_layout (the decoder's position rows under the learner's position_rows, and the finger rows): x y z of every row outside those rows (12 rows under 'all', the eyes' row included) and the radius of all 26 rows are copied from the iteration-0 composite (computed by init) in every assembled candidate; masked_execution holds the same numbers after planned_execution and the hand stage; _plan_chain passes the layout at both constructions and wraps the route's execution transform, so the one masked command enters transition() and the body forecast. executed_fields_only stays off; learned weights and the head's 9-number input are unchanged.
- Recording (no command, loss, gradient or selection change): forecast_pose__{iteration0,selected}_{position_cm,quaternion,order}, forecast_pose__target, and the hand state (plus1/end hand hinge angles and velocities, hand_joint_goal_raw) in the existing model-lane capture entry; PLAN_CAPTURE_DEFINITIONS explains them, including that an accepted capture is on disk only after the lane writes its chunk.
- Independent review: ACCEPT WITH CHANGES (no blocker) on 82dbf4d1f and 6facfeadb, and again on 66889bdba; every change applied. Its reading: the post-execution mask changes no value today (the raw pin already holds the numbers) and guards against a future transform that mixes rows.
- Checks at e058c0c81: s1_planned_live_identity_check PASS, 10 of 10 (the planner's executed form equals the live step's on the 25 body rows bit for bit, with production's eye-row options; the command gradients equal the f0183150b form's exactly; the former form's difference is detected). decoder_inert_fields_check PASS, 16 of 16 (no candidate changes or sends a gradient through an inert number, before or after execution; the first composite is unchanged; the whole score is independent of them; with a head that only inert numbers can move, the real search loop falls back to iteration 0 where the former assembly changed them; the recorded forecasts belong to exactly the commands the head read and reach the lane entry).
- Risk to inherited training (the review's reading): no weight, optimizer, buffer, episode companion or start state changes; the trainer code hash changes, so the configuration is new (d7dbfb994bea86f0); planner-latched commands now carry the controller's radius and inert x y z into the ledger, the motor encoder, replay and the body head's lesson (in a1 the Adam search could set the radius anywhere in [0, 1] and move inert x y z by up to 1.80 cm; the preceding trust_v2 block never searched those numbers); S1 moves planned positions by at most one float32 unit; unmeasured: how many more bodies now fall back to the iteration-0 command.
- Outside these decisions (the review's note): the causal chain's perturbed alternatives add noise to every row's x y z, inert rows included, so their recorded forecasts include the head's response to numbers no actuator reads.

2. OWNER (repair package; logic b986ff6e, path-stepped for a2 as f51c5c34 with launch-wiring constants and text only):
- The wall-cap stop request exactly 178 s before the 720 s cap, by the monitor and by the guard's backstop (both aligned). The kill no earlier than the acknowledgement's whole-second name + 1 s + 84 s once writing is seen (the temporary snapshot folder, the companion's temporary file, or a complete snapshot after the acknowledgement), never after the cap; the floor is fixed by the acknowledgement and never moved by file growth.
- The monitor, the guard and the closing wait on one schedule: the closing wait starts from the saved schedules (the guard saves its own in guard_schedule.json), and a first look already past the kill time takes a second look 5 s later.
- A preservation-risk report (one owner event and the arm-end field) when the acknowledgement leaves too little time and when no acknowledgement comes before the kill; saving is never claimed as guaranteed.
- Detail-record flush verification after the trainer's end, read only, per capture durable or not, in detail_flush.json and the arm-end receipt. A clean snapshot_and_stop exit closes the plan capture and the observer lanes after "Checkpoint saved"; a forced kill flushes nothing.
- Reviews: c2489775 found a BLOCKER (the closing wait started a fresh schedule; on the late-acknowledgement timing it would end the tree at acknowledgement + 63-68 s, repeating a1) and three timing changes; e5dff718 two changes; b986ff6e ACCEPT.
- Check pose_learning_late_ack_schedule_check2 PASS, 46 of 46 conditions: actual timing, kill at 4:28:05.1 PM PDT (request + 178 s); late acknowledgement at the request + 120 s, kill at 4:28:32.0 PM PDT (acknowledgement + 84.88 s); acknowledgement too late, kill exactly at the cap with the risk report; the closing wait, the guard and the monitor's stale first look hold the floor; a1's 7 captures not durable; the measurement run's captures durable. Its first run (row pose_learning_late_ack_schedule_check) was INVALID: the check program refused its own registered evidence folder and evaluated nothing; follow-up written, the output guard narrowed to the protected folders only, one rerun.
- Residuals: with no guard schedule and a quiet save stretch of more than 5 s, the monitor's stale first look could still end the tree early (it needs a monitor hang of 178 s or more and a dead guard); the floor leaves 8.2-9.2 s after a measured save and exit, and the interpreter's own exit time is unmeasured.

3. ARM GEOMETRY (your second finding): the launched search's per-handle forecast poses were never saved: the capture lines hold per-body position and rotation sums only, and a1's observer model folder holds only a header. The recording above adds them going forward. Saved per-handle forecasts exist only as the body head's tenure forecasts of EXECUTED commands in earlier runs' observer chunks (S4R_measure_496000: 51 records, all arm handles and the chest, measured poses at start and end), from the lesson route and the sensory search on code d6a12e317: usable only to read back the composition rule, not the launched search. Smallest plan (readback only, one registered row, no fresh run, no new predictor, no projection): compose each saved forecast with forecast_pose's rule and report, against the measured poses and the scene geometry, the shoulder and upper-arm link residuals, the elbow hinge's off-axis turn and range, the forearm-to-hand distance against its recorded range, and each origin's height against the floor, with the same composition of the achieved change as the noise floor; shoulder and wrist joint limits not tested. Disclosure: two inventory reads of saved arrays (the join of forecasts to measured poses, the reference geometry) were made without a registry row; their numbers are not used as results.

4. PACKAGE a2 (DRAFT, repair package; prepared after the source was pinned; a1 and its frozen package untouched):
- Attempts s4r_pose_learning_496250_a2 and s4r_pose_learning_496250_reading_a2, run S4R_pose_learning_a2_496250, a new preservation destination, all absent.
- command.json ed55e240... (exactly 4 output-path tokens differ from 2ddab089...); configuration d7dbfb994bea86f0 (only the 4 changed code files differ from 2819b74cc6afc95c's code hash).
- The seventh ADOPTION_ROUTES entry drafted unbound (fingerprint and decision None, as the sixth before binding) with its test delta; not applied to main.
- Owner f51c5c34...; reader 74c21047...; adapted launch helpers; gates draft with all seven FAIL, carried from 2819b74cc6afc95c with the new evidence and no repair claimed; manifest DRAFT b7e95ba9... (62 pins, all hash equal).
- The owner's launch preconditions read statically: 19 PASS, 6 WAIT (the preflight record, the two Tests rows, applying and binding the seventh entry, the adoption file, the binding receipt), 0 REFUSE.
- The pinned worktree is now a full checkout: my sparse one lacked the watcher's files under docs/, which now match the launched checkout's byte for byte.
- Independent package review: ACCEPT WITH CHANGES, nothing unsafe and no training authority; one stale dependency note and one overstatement in the gates draft (gate 6) corrected.
- Not done, awaiting your package decision: writing the preflight record d7dbfb994bea86f0 (its dry run computes the fingerprint; no record exists yet), registering the two a2 rows, applying the unbound seventh entry with its test delta to main and one focused adoption check, binding, freezing the manifest and the binding receipt.

5. FINDINGS: a1 recorded a 30 s scheduled video at 4:24:52 PM PDT and a moment video at 4:24:59 PM PDT inside the block (the launched plan said none would fire); a2 keeps the video flags unchanged. At the slowest measured pace the wall-cap stop's floor lands after the cap, which gives a risk report although a measured save would finish before the cap.

DECISIONS NEEDED (yours):
1. Whether a capture whose detail records are not durable fails the block (today it is recorded, not a failure).
2. --observer-chunk-steps (default 100; not in the command): lower it so capture arrays reach disk before a forced stop in a block of at most 100 model steps? It changes the configuration fingerprint.
3. Whether the block keeps its video flags.
4. The geometry readback plan above, as one registered readback.
5. The a2 package: the record and rows, the unbound seventh entry with one focused adoption check, then your binding and launch decision. No training authority is asked here.
